text:
michael: Quick sync — we need to reconcile the autoscaler <> pool-operator contract for Dedicated GPU pools. Gaps I see: who owns headroom accounting, the fallback matrix when capacity is constrained, and the admission vs throttling API surface. Any immediate concerns?

shreya: +1. We should define a clean split: autoscaler owns intent (desired nodes + headroom estimation) and the operator owns allocation/execution/prewarm. Autoscaler exposes an 'intent' object with reason + TTL so operator can make deterministic decisions.

nate: Question: if the operator can't allocate (e.g., preemptible nodes lost), what should autoscaler do? immediate scale-up, route to hosted, or throttle? Need explicit fallback semantics.

eva: Propose a versioned fallback matrix keyed by tenant QoS -> action (wait, queue, model-variant, route-hosted). Operator should consult the matrix when it cannot satisfy intent.

shreya: Draft API sketch for autoscaler -> operator intent (WIP):
```json
{
  "intent": {
    "pool": "dedicated-gpu-a",
    "desired_nodes": 12,
    "headroom_pct": 18,
    "reason": "traffic_spike",
    "ttl_sec": 300,
    "fallback": [
      {"tier":"platinum","action":"queued"},
      {"tier":"gold","action":"route-hosted"},
      {"tier":"standard","action":"serve-quantized"}
    ]
  }
}
```

paul: +1 to versioned fallback. Also need metering hooks so we don't double-bill when requests are routed to hosted endpoints as fallback. Billing team needs a signal.

deploy-bot: deploy started: ded-pool-operator v2 -> canary (3/3)

michael: Quick API question — should tenants request a 'lease' from operator before sending traffic, or should autoscaler provide an 'admit' token? Which reduces headroom variance?

shreya: I'd lean lease API on operator: POST /v1/pools/{pool}/lease?count=1 -> returns token + expiry. Pros: operator controls allocation granularity and TTL. Cons: extra round-trip.

nate: Lease is fine. We can optimize by piggybacking on LB health checks and batching lease calls. Need idempotent issuance.

eva: Another edge: when fallback action is 'serve-quantized', operator must ensure model variant compatibility and KV cache continuity. We'll need a variant mapping table per model pinned by version.

paul: From ops side: surface these telemetry signals — admission_rejections_total, fallback_rate{action,tier}, lease_issue_latency_seconds. Those will feed cost and SLO dashboards.

michael: Action items: shreya -> draft intent+lease proto; eva -> enumerate fallback matrix with variant compatibility; nate -> spec telemetry + idempotency; paul -> billing hook design. Target: EOD Friday. @shreya @eva @nate @paul

shreya: I'll open a PR with the proto + example client snippet.

eva: I'll drop the fallback matrix doc here: https://internal/redwood/dedicated/fallback-matrix (WIP)

nate: I'll add Prometheus metric names & example dashboards to the repo.

paul: I'll sync with metering on the billing signal and add a short runbook for hosted-reroute billing.

michael: Thanks — once PRs land we should reconvene and update the formal RFC with the operator/admission surface.

shreya: ack, thanks everyone :)

paul: FYI: if anyone needs the canary results from operator v2, ping me and I'll share logs.

michael: closing for now — moved to RFC follow-up thread after artifacts are uploaded.
